items.title: Bournemouth make European history after coming from behind to beat Celta Vigo
items.excerpt: Bournemouth continued their magnificent run of form with a 2-1 victory against Celta Vigo, creating two bits of history in the process.
body: Bournemouth continued their magnificent run of form with a 2-1 victory against Celta Vigo, creating two bits of history in the process.

It was a club-record-extending 10th successive win for Bournemouth in all competitions, with the victory also marking the first time an English club have won their first five matches in major European competition. Veteran former Liverpool striker Iago Aspas put the home side in front in style in the first half, before Bournemouth were reduced to 10 men when Bafode Diakite was sent off for a late challenge.

items.title: Hemmings unfazed by rise at Villa and eager to take next step
items.excerpt: Two days after being thrown into a cauldron in Istanbul during Aston Villa's loss to Galatasaray in the Champions League, George Hemmings strolls into the media centre at Bodymoor Heath, sliders on, looking entirely at home in the senior su…
body: Two days after being thrown into a cauldron in Istanbul during Aston Villa's loss to Galatasaray in the Champions League, George Hemmings strolls into the media centre at Bodymoor Heath, sliders on, looking entirely at home in the senior surroundings that should be new to him.
The nineteen-year-old is quiet and reserved to start but soon settled into proceedings when quizzed on that atmosphere and what the experience was like.

"It was mad," he says with a smile on his face. "When we had the ball, you couldn't hear anything but whistling." items.title: Eckert: Time to 'close the chapter' on Spygate ahead of Boro reunion
items.excerpt: "I think we've experienced a little bit more in the last 12 months than normal."
body: "I think we've experienced a little bit more in the last 12 months than normal."
It may be the understatement of the century, but it's not a huge surprise considering Tonda Eckert is a relatively understated man.

The storm of 'Spygate' is over, but the aftershock is still being felt. Southampton are sixth in the table, seven points behind leaders Middlesbrough ahead of their reunion on Friday night - live on Sky Sports .

Were it not for the four-point deduction, the gap would be smaller. Were it not for the entire controversy, the Saints would possibly be in the Premier League right now. items.title: SFA to deliver revised proposal after young player vote delayed
items.excerpt: The Scottish FA will continue to consult with SPFL clubs about youth development after initial plans failed to reach a member vote.
body: The Scottish FA will continue to consult with SPFL clubs about youth development after initial plans failed to reach a member vote.
At a summit in September, Scottish football's governing body proposed financial incentives and penalties along with quotas , in a bid to get more homegrown talent playing for Scottish clubs.

Initially, the plans were to have been voted on at an SFA general meeting in October and the SPFL's annual meeting this month. items.title: Chelsea Q&A: Are Blues in crisis? What next for Fofana after viral interview?
items.excerpt: After Chelsea fell to back-to-back losses with a 4-1 humiliation by Leeds at Stamford Bridge last Saturday, Sky Sports News reporter James Savundra examines the latest developments at Stamford Bridge.
body: After Chelsea fell to back-to-back losses with a 4-1 humiliation by Leeds at Stamford Bridge last Saturday, Sky Sports News reporter James Savundra examines the latest developments at Stamford Bridge.

As well as suffering a third defeat in four Premier League games, Chelsea and manager Xabi Alonso also faced the added frustration of defender Wesley Fofana giving an unauthorised interview this week, in which he laughed off his penalty miss in last month's Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool and revealed he had contemplated retiring during his time at Stamford Bridge.
